insight: Content-write primitives must deny git metadata (.git, case-insensitive): writing bytes then running git is a code-execution path.
Cache the remote manifest's own content_key/updated_at; local wall-clock timestamps cannot decide whether a pulled record changed.
Sub-agent briefs must scope files explicitly: three parallel agents on disjoint paths kept 1 100+ tests green while the orchestrator wrote the engine.

A settings surface that never reads back what it stored is a silent lie: applyFormToInputs never repopulated the ssh.* fields (so a saved local-clone path was invisible, and the next syncForm read the blank field as no-path), and the auth-mode picker was filled from defaults at first paint so it could never show a stored ssh mode. Found only when a feature had to render that state.

A per-store tier belongs in the store: return the missing .omnipilot/config.json and let the caller commit carry it (extraFiles), so the same write primitive both makes the repository self-describing and refuses to overwrite a recorded mode. Committing it separately changed four existing assertions; riding an existing commit changed none.
A capability with no entry point is, to the user, absent: capture mode 'note' was typed, validated and handled for months while no surface could send it, so the feature read as unsupported.

A waived layer is only honest when the gap it leaves is named in the report: E2E was skipped by explicit user instruction, so the residual risk (popup wiring) is written down with a manual acceptance step instead of being silently absent.
